result.topic_en: Ramanujan begins section 18, deriving an expression for the generating series of the divisor function $\sigma_{s-1}(n)$ from the partial-fraction expansion of $\pi\coth\pi x$ differentiated $s-1$ times, aiming at asymptotics for large $s$.
result.transcription:
18. I shall conclude this paper by finding an expression
for
$\sum_1^\infty \sigma_s(n) x^n, \quad \sum_1^\infty r_s(n) x^n$
which shows the asymptotic nature for large values of $s$.
If $R(x)>0$, $R(x)$ being the real part of $x$, it is well
known that
(18.1) $\pi + 2\pi(e^{-2\pi x}+e^{-4\pi x}+e^{-6\pi x}+\cdots)$
$= \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x+i}+\frac{1}{x-i}+\frac{1}{x+2i}+\frac{1}{x-2i}+\cdots.$
Differentiating the two sides in (18.1) $s-1$ times we
obtain
(18.11) $1^{s-1}e^{-2\pi x}+2^{s-1}e^{-4\pi x}+3^{s-1}e^{-6\pi x}+\cdots$
$=\frac{\Gamma(s)}{(2\pi)^s}\left\{\frac{1}{x^s}+\frac{1}{(x+i)^s}+\frac{1}{(x-i)^s}+\frac{1}{(x+2i)^s}+\cdots\right\}$
if $s$ is [-a positive-] an integer greater than 1. This re-
sult is quite elementary. But it can be shown by
the theory of residues that (18.11) is true for all values
of $s$ greater than 1. It follows from this that
$\sum_1^\infty \sigma_{s-1}(n)e^{-2\pi n x} = \sum_1^\infty (1^{s-1}e^{-2\pi n x}+2^{s-1}e^{-4\pi n x}+\cdots)$
$=\frac{\Gamma(s)}{(2\pi)^s}\sum_1^\infty\left\{\frac{1}{(nx)^s}+\frac{1}{(nx+i)^s}+\frac{1}{(nx-i)^s}+\cdots\right\}$
The double series in the last equation is absolutely
convergent if $s>2$. From this we easily deduce that
(18.2) $\sigma_{s-1}(1)e^{-2\pi x}+\sigma_{s-1}(2)e^{-4\pi x}+\cdots$
$=\frac{\Gamma(s)}{(2\pi)^s}\zeta(s)\left\{\frac{1}{x^s}+\sum\frac{1}{(\mu x+\nu i)^s}+\sum\frac{1}{(\mu x-\nu i)^s}\right\}$

methods.what: Partial-fraction (Mittag-Leffler) expansion of $\pi\coth\pi x$ for Re x > 0
Lipschitz-type summation formula obtained by differentiating s-1 times
Extension of the formula to real s>1 via residue theory

methods.what: Eisenstein-series-type expression for the divisor generating function, with factor $\zeta(s)$ and sums over lattice points
